_comment: Where each 500M recipe value came from. A value being set is not provenance;
each entry names the artifact that determined it. Written by fb 2026-09-01,
who ruled each one, because nobody else holds the sources.

Values not on this list were not chosen for this run and keep their Cfg defaults. A value PASSED on the command line must be on this list: the launch_command gate reconciles argv against these keys, and a flag with no entry here reads as a knob turned for no recorded reason. warmdown/anneal_frac/warmup/save_every were passed but unlisted until e1-9.

_not_chosen.fone: off — the mechanism is real but the target capability is short executable functions, not arithmetic. e1 runs the A/B in parallel under a three-band rule whose middle band is a reportable 'not decidable at this budget' (f30ca74).
_not_chosen.attn_res: Full, on — user order 2026-09-01, no retest. The A/B was run at 200M; the transfer risk is accepted. attn_res_blocks=8 is the lever in reserve if memory ever forces it, and it is a Cfg value, not a code change.
_not_chosen.tokenizer: not rebuilt — every veto gate passes and the case rested on a compression metric whose documented correlation with downstream reaches -0.09. e1's framing, adopted: rebuilding would be accepting an unmeasured bet, not following the metrics.

_partitioned_by_shape: TWO RECIPES, ONE FILE, KEYED BY SHAPE (b0 2026-09-03, 6e authorised). This file was flat and described the 493.6M L32 run only. gate_recipe_provenance then returned GO for a 206M L12 launch, truthfully -- it asks whether each value HAS a source, not whether the source is about the model being launched -- so twelve entries arguing for another shape read as twelve justified values. scripts/test_e2e.py:59 had already written the hazard down ('recipe_provenance's 32 belongs to the 500M run and would silently turn an 8-step smoke test into a 500M one') without the file being able to express the distinction. The gate is not weakened by this; it is given something shape-specific to read.

493.6M-L32.dim: 1024 — held at today's width deliberately. Instantiating the real HybridLM on a meta device gave 493.6M at L32; three later constructions (tilerl, de) agree. Holding width fixed removes the LR width-transfer axis entirely, which was the largest launch risk (fb ruling, board shape_recipe 2026-09-01).
493.6M-L32.layers: 32 — the whole parameter increase goes into depth (user order 2026-09-01). d/L 32.0 against the ~45 CompleteP calls compute-optimal at this size: deliberately deeper. Stated to the user as an unsupported bet, not a derivation: 44's survey found no published measurement of depth against free-running agreement in either direction (docs/lessons/trajectory_calibration_survey.md).
493.6M-L32.heads: 8 — forced, not chosen. FlashKDA's CUTLASS kernel is compiled for head_dim 128, so heads = dim/128. train.py refuses a mismatched pair rather than failing inside the kernel (a52e074).
493.6M-L32.ffn_hidden: 3072 — 3x width, unchanged from the 200M runs. Width did not move, so this constant did not have to.
493.6M-L32.batch: 32 — measured. tilerl's compiled batch fit: 32 fits at world=1 (63.95 GiB), 64 does not. The earlier 16 was an EAGER measurement quoted for hours before Cfg.compile was noticed; compile roughly doubles the ceiling in both grad_ckpt arms (probes/t66_depth_shape.py@4016bdc).
493.6M-L32.accum: 1 -- arithmetic, not a measurement: batch 32 at world 8 gives 8 x 32 x 4096 = 1,048,576 tokens per step (user ruling 2026-09-02, was world 7 / 917,504). The earlier value matched the 200M runs' tok/step exactly so 44's matched-token axis needed no conversion; at world 8 it no longer does and that axis must convert or be abandoned -- the value is unchanged, half its reason is not. The memory alternative b16+accum2 reaches the same tok/step at 36.29 GiB against 69.63, recorded in runs/memory_peaks.json as 7_alt_b16a2, and is reserve for longer seq, not a fallback (b0 caught the stale clause and the untracked citation, 2026-09-02).
493.6M-L32.lr_scale: 0.85 — b0's t71 measured the depth exponent 12->32 at +0.141 +/- 0.011 over 9 runs, against the 1/sqrt(L) rule's +0.500, so 0.61 was a 2.3x over-correction. Both premises of that rule fail here: AttnRes makes the residual stream a convex combination (sum of softmax weights = 1 at every q scale, so no depth growth to cancel), and Muon normalises away the gradient-magnitude tracking the exponent is derived from. 0.877 is the bound; 0.85 is inside it, chosen because a too-high LR fails loudly in the first 500 steps and a too-low one looks like a healthy run that quietly underperforms (b88de6c, verified by fb running its selftest against the real train.py). The asymmetry is not two symmetric bad outcomes: too high shows up as a loss spike or a gradient-norm blowup in the first 500 steps and is observable; too low produces a curve that looks entirely healthy and simply ends lower than it should, and we have no control run that would reveal it. One failure shouts, the other does not (tilerl).
493.6M-L32.grad_ckpt: true — measured, and it inverts with depth. At L=32 checkpointing costs 1.116x per step and gives 4x the batch at LESS peak memory; the 2.4x cost that ruled it out at L=12 was measured against accum 1, which is not the choice at this depth. Stored activations dominate at depth, which is exactly the regime where trading all of them for one recompute wins (eff.grad_ckpt_inverts_with_depth, bc65b15).
493.6M-L32.warmdown: 0.1 -- the WSD tail, and the one value whose omission is a 6.5x error rather than a nuisance. Cfg defaults to 0.65, which at 19,073 steps starts the cosine descent at step 6,676 = 13.00B tokens instead of step 17,166 = 2.00B (tilerl's arithmetic, docs/lessons/gate_failure_shapes.md shape 28). Launched value read from the register row for this run (runs/experiments.jsonl, p500m_20b_0902, status running).
493.6M-L32.anneal_frac: 0 -- no anneal phase, matching the stage-1 WSD join of docs/lessons/readout_30b_prereg.md:110 (`--warmdown 0 --anneal_frac 0`). Recorded even though its omission is HARMLESS here: all nine domains of data/mix_500m.json have |weight - anneal| == 0, so the two phases compose identically and a missing flag changes row order only. Listed so the gate can tell 'passed' from 'defaulted' -- which is not the same question as whether it mattered.
493.6M-L32.warmup: 300 absolute steps, not a fraction: a fractional warmup lost 0.52 val at the 0.2B point (facts/efficiency.json#eff.warmup_absolute_not_fractional). Same 300 as the 30B recipe (docs/lessons/readout_30b_prereg.md:15). Cfg defaults to 20 = 0.105% of this run, and that fallback shipped once on 2026-09-02 without an error.
493.6M-L32.save_every: 500 steps -- measured, and the key this file was missing until e1-9 (2026-09-02). t38 measured a 959MB checkpoint write at 4.91s median cold, so 500 steps is ~15 min = 0.55% of wall and caps crash loss at one interval; the floor is ~8 min to keep the write under 1% (facts/efficiency.json#eff.ckpt_resume_16h_interval). Cfg/argparse defaults to 1000. Launched value read from runs/experiments.jsonl, p500m_20b_0902.
493.6M-L32._shape: 493.6M d1024 L32 h8 ffn3072, world 8, 20B tokens
493.6M-L32._note: Unchanged from the flat file fb wrote 2026-09-01, moved verbatim under its shape. Nothing here was re-ruled; the only edit is that it now says which model it argues for.

206M-L12.dim: 1024 -- the ANCHOR width, and the leg's whole point is that it does not move. This leg answers 'params or data', and the params leg is the one that changes shape; holding d fixed here is what makes the two legs comparable. Instantiating the real HybridLM gives 206,128,200 params at L12 (the figure runs/experiments.jsonl records for every ab_* arm, e.g. ab_value_embed's measured 206,128,200 -> 239,788,104).
206M-L12.layers: 12 -- the anchor depth, NOT a choice made for this leg. Every ab_* speedrun arm runs d1024 L12 (scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh:105), so the data leg sits on a shape with a measured tok/s, a measured peak, and a measured loss curve. Depth is also why the PARAMS leg must widen rather than deepen: model.py places MLA at i %% attn_every == attn_every-1, so L12 is 3 MLA / 9 KDA and L18 would be 4/14 -- deepening changes the MLA:KDA ratio and stops being a pure parameter change.
206M-L12.heads: 8 -- forced, not chosen, same reason as at L32: FlashKDA's CUTLASS kernel is compiled for head_dim 128, so heads = dim/128 and train.py refuses a mismatched pair rather than failing inside the kernel.
206M-L12.ffn_hidden: 3072 -- 3x width, the anchor's value. Width did not move, so this constant did not have to.
206M-L12.batch: 16 -- the anchor arms' measured value (scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh:105), NOT the L32 recipe's 32. Reused rather than re-measured because a peak for exactly this pair already exists: runs/memory_peaks.json world 4 records 61.01 GiB at b16 accum2 with 34.57 GiB headroom, read off the A/B (2a) baseline arm that ran this configuration. The L32 entry's 32 came from a COMPILED fit at world=1 on a different depth and does not transfer.
206M-L12.accum: 2 -- arithmetic, not a measurement: 16 x 2 x 4 cards x 4096 = 524,288 tokens per step at world 4. Paired with batch 16 because that is the pair the anchor arms ran and the pair runs/memory_peaks.json has a peak for; b32a1 at this depth has no measured peak at any world size.
206M-L12.lr_scale: 1.0 -- the anchor's value, and at L12 it is the un-scaled baseline rather than a correction. The L32 entry's 0.85 IS a depth correction (b0's t71 measured the 12->32 exponent at +0.141), so its whole justification is a move away from L12; carrying 0.85 onto an L12 leg would apply a depth correction for a depth change that is not happening. Every ab_* arm runs lr_scale 1.0 (scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh:106).
206M-L12.grad_ckpt: false -- and this INVERTS with depth, which is exactly why it cannot be inherited from the L32 entry. facts/efficiency.json#eff.grad_ckpt_inverts_with_depth: at L=32 checkpointing costs 1.116x per step and wins on memory; the 2.4x cost that ruled it out at L=12 is the L12 measurement, and L12 is this leg. It also fits without it: 61.01 GiB peak, 34.57 GiB headroom (runs/memory_peaks.json world 4). Passed as --no-grad_ckpt, which is BooleanOptionalAction's explicit off, not an omission.
206M-L12.warmdown: 0.1 -- the WSD tail, same value and same reason as the L32 recipe: Cfg defaults to 0.65, which would start the cosine descent at 13%% of the run instead of 90%%. This is the value whose omission is a 6.5x error rather than a nuisance (docs/lessons/gate_failure_shapes.md shape 28). The anchor arms pass 0.1 (scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh:106).
206M-L12.anneal_frac: 0 -- no anneal phase. Harmless here for a reason that is CHECKED rather than inherited: all nine domains of data/mix_200m_8b.json have |weight - anneal| == 0, so the two phases compose identically and a missing flag would change row order only. Listed so the gate can tell 'passed' from 'defaulted', which is not the same question as whether it mattered.
206M-L12.warmup: 300 absolute steps, not a fraction: a fractional warmup lost 0.52 val at the 0.2B point (facts/efficiency.json#eff.warmup_absolute_not_fractional). Same 300 as the anchor arms (scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh:106) and the 30B recipe. Cfg defaults to 20, and that fallback shipped once on 2026-09-02 without an error.
206M-L12.save_every: 500 steps -- t38 measured a 959MB write at 4.91s median cold, so 500 steps caps crash loss at one interval while keeping the write well under 1%% of wall (facts/efficiency.json#eff.ckpt_resume_16h_interval). A 206M checkpoint is SMALLER than the 959MB that figure was measured on, so the cost bound holds with margin rather than by extrapolation. Note the .stepN files this produces hold the NaN-rollback buffer and can lag their own name by up to min(200, save_every) steps: at 500 that is -100 on alternating files (docs/lessons/gate_failure_shapes.md shape 139).
206M-L12._shape: 206.1M d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072, world 4, 8.000B tokens (data leg)
206M-L12._note: Written by b0 2026-09-03, authorised by 6e. NOT a copy of the L32 group with numbers changed: five of the twelve differ (layers, batch, accum, lr_scale, grad_ckpt) and each of those five differs BECAUSE the L32 entry's own justification is depth-specific -- 0.85 is a 12->32 correction, grad_ckpt inverts with depth, batch 32 came from a compiled fit at another depth. A value whose reason names L32 cannot be inherited by an L12 leg just because the number would still parse. Every citation here names a TRACKED file: the peak's own source log lives only on the pod, so it is cited through runs/memory_peaks.json, which now carries its numbers and its provenance.
